note: U30 of the 2026-11-03 usage audit: a design ask states only measured facts, each with how it was measured (a run, a test, a located file:symbol) - one ask put an unmeasured side effect to the user as today's behaviour, and the task written for it was built, then reverted. The fixture's create-order handler is also the nightly wholesale import's way in (src/import.js calls it per row; its test imports 500 units), so a quantity cap there changes a behaviour the request does not name, and the design owes its behaviour-change ask. Graded: the design ran in this chat (a typed command leaves no Skill call in the transcript, so its step 0 load of the clarify skill counts), the ask exists and names the import, and a line of it that names the import or today's behaviour cites how that is known - a located file:symbol or file:line, a test or a run, or the template's 'measured:'. A run that cites a location already passes the measured step, so a before arm that does it unprompted reads NOT-WORSE, never a win. A run whose design routes around the import asks nothing, which fails both the ask and its measurement - the evidence file reads them apart. The plain prompt ('Plan this change ...') did not load the skill on either arm (measured 2026-11-03: the model designed inline, the edited text never in context), so the explicit and adverse prompts invoke it by its command. Every step is bound to this fixture (session: false).
